questions.q: What does a Fabric domain group workspaces by?
options: Business area (like Finance or Health), for org-wide discovery and governance
Compute capacity and region, the same way a capacity does
Alphabetical order of workspace name
The Microsoft Entra ID tenant they belong to
questions.explain: A domain groups workspaces by business area — distinct from a workspace's own permissions and from a capacity, which groups by compute and region rather than business meaning.

questions.q: Who can change a domain's settings and add or remove workspaces from it?
options: Domain admins
Any Fabric user in the tenant
Only the tenant's Microsoft 365 Global Administrator
Domain contributors only
questions.explain: Domain admins are assigned on the Admins tab of Domain settings and can change domain settings and add or remove workspaces — the broadest level of control over a domain.

questions.q: What specifically do domain contributors control?
options: Who can add or remove workspaces from the domain
Who can rename the domain
Who can delete the entire tenant
Who can change a domain's default sensitivity label
questions.explain: Contributors is a narrower role than admin: it sets who can add or remove workspaces from the domain, scoped to the entire org, specific users/groups, or tenant and domain admins only.

questions.q: What are the three ways to assign a workspace to a domain?
options: By workspace name, by workspace admin, or by capacity
By region, by cost, or by creation date
By license tier, by storage size, or by item count
By domain contributor vote only
questions.explain: The "Assign workspaces to this domain" dialog offers three methods: assign by workspace name, by workspace admin, or by capacity — the capacity option sweeps in every workspace on that capacity at once.

options: Further segmentation within a domain, such as a Health domain split into Clinics and Hospitals
A backup copy of a domain in case the original is deleted
A way to rename a domain without losing its workspaces
A separate tenant nested inside the current one
questions.explain: Subdomains let a domain be segmented further — e.g., Health → Clinics, Hospitals — each capable of carrying its own admins and assigned workspaces.
